The '''Battle of Congrave''' was the central urban battle of the [[Solara-Khalindar War]]. It included Khalindar's 1990 capture of [[Congrave]] and Solara's 1992 campaign to retake the capital.

== First Battle ==

After the attack on [[Albroke]], Khalindar targeted Congrave to damage Solaran command, morale, and political continuity. Khalindarian forces used naval operations to force access to the city's port approaches, then landed troops and heavy equipment.

The fighting became urban and close-range. Solaran soldiers, police, and civilian volunteers fortified buildings, barricades, transport hubs, communications centers, and government districts. Khalindarian forces advanced through the city with heavy casualties on both sides.

Old source material states that Congrave fell after roughly three weeks of combat. The fall of the capital was one of the deepest shocks in modern Solaran history.

== Occupation And Defense ==

Khalindarian forces fortified the city after its capture, using government buildings, industrial districts, port areas, and road junctions as defensive nodes. Mines, barricades, sniper positions, and strongpoints made the city difficult to retake.

The occupation also created a civilian crisis. Basic services were disrupted, buildings were destroyed, and evacuation became dangerous.

== Recapture ==

In 1992, Solara launched a counteroffensive to retake Congrave after gaining air superiority during the [[Battle of Solara]]. The operation combined airstrikes, amphibious landings south of the city, infantry assaults, special forces actions, artillery, armor, and combat engineers.

The campaign lasted roughly two months. Solaran forces cleared the government district, industrial sector, and port area while the [[Bay of Congrave]] engagement weakened Khalindarian resupply.

By mid-June 1992, Solara declared Congrave recaptured. The victory became the turning point of the land war and restored Solaran morale after the disasters of 1990.

== Legacy ==

Congrave connected the war's political cause and military consequences. It was the city where Solara had hosted the 1940 agreement with Khalindar, the capital Khalindar tried to seize for a quick victory, and the symbol Solara had to retake to prove national survival.
